newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Bucaram appeals to military for support.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Bucaram appeals to military for support.

text.p: Ecuador's Abdala Bucaram issued an appeal for support from the military on Thursday after an extraordinary session of Congress voted to oust him on grounds of mental incompetence.
In a statement issued to the military high command, read on national television by his press secretary, a defiant Bucaram said he remained the country's only democratically elected president.

The statement slammed the 44-34 vote to impeach him as "anti-democratic and in violation of constitutional norms," and said Bucaram, who remained firm, "had no intention of abandoning the presidential palace."

There was no statement from the army high command, but troops in combat gear reinforced positions around the presidential palace shortly after it was read in an apparent bid to protect it from thousands of angry protesters demanding Bucaram's removal.
Bucaram had warned earlier on Thursday that he would use "all the powers available to protect the legitimacy of the popular will and national judicial order."

The tumultuous congressional session ousting Bucaram came on the second day of a 48-hour general strike called by unions to oppose the harsh economic austerity measures that Bucaram clamped on Ecuador last month.
